source.paper: Wessinger & Rausher (2014) Predictability and irreversibility of genetic changes associated with flower color evolution in Penstemon barbatus
source.table: Table 1: Flower colour phenotype x F3′5′h genotype in 161 interspecific F2 individuals
source.source_kind: published peer-reviewed article Table 1, manually transcribed and arithmetic checked
source.analysis_type: retrospective public-text count replication; no new source experiment

trait_target: blue-purple delphinidin-based floral colour; P. barbatus remains RED and anthocyanin-pigmented, not a white flower or total pigment loss

genotype_definition.Ff: one allele from each parental lineage

reported_source_molecular_results.experiment: Recombinant P. barbatus F3′5′H enzyme did not show detectable activity; converting its premature termination codon back to glycine did not restore enzyme activity; at least one additional structural substitution is implicated.

inference_ceiling: Genetic crossing with a donor species is an experimental gain of the donor allele, not endogenous re-evolution of the damaged P. barbatus gene.
The trait is loss of the blue-purple pigment branch while red anthocyanin pigmentation remains present.
Source F2 counts do not establish real-world hybrid gene flow or population establishment.
Repair of one nonsense codon not restoring catalytic activity demonstrates additional source biochemical problem but does not identify every lesion.
Published authors' genotype-phenotype results are background evidence, not independent new user-collected ecological replication.
One interspecific cross of a particular locus cannot calibrate cross-angiosperm restoration hazard or ANTO v10 parameters.

comparison_units.Penstemon: one published original experimental programme (one genus)
comparison_units.Petunia: one separate regain clade, independently published prior evidence
comparison_units.Ryukyu_Cirsium: unverified candidate with prospective same-plant function

prespecified_new_hypothesis: Future phenotype accessibility conditional on structurally intact functional modules and their provenance can diverge sharply from observed historical phenotype state; donor-mediated restoration and endogenous repair are distinct mechanisms.
